text.p: Rehabilicare Inc said Monday it continues to spend heavily on marketing its CTDx systems and expects to see positive results of the marketing in the second half of fiscal 1997.
"We have also continued to invest heavily in marketing this product to industry," David Kaysen, president and chief executive, said of CTDx, used for repetitive stress injuries.
"We expect positive results from our efforts in this key arena in the near future," Kaysen said in a statement.

Earlier, Rehabilicare, which provides electromedical pain management and rehabilitaion products and service, reported earnings for its second fiscal quarter ended December 31 of $0.03 a share, versus $0.02 a share the previous year.
The company said its CTDx posted a 78 percent sales increase over the first quarter.

Rehabilicare said its core retail and domestic wholesale businesses are "solidly back on a growth track", and it expects its international wholesale business to grow, with initiatives underway in England and Germany.
"The second quarter results have laid a very solid foundation for the balance of fiscal 1997 and beyond," Kaysen said.
